Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-20.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2019-25786
CVE.report.description: Gnuboard5 5.0.1 before 5.3.3.3 and 5.4.0.1 before 5.4.0.2 contains a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to inject scripts through the arr_ajax_msg parameter. Attackers can craft GET requests to /plugin/sms5/ajax.sms_emoticon.php, where common.php's @extract($_GET) injects the value into the echoed JSON output, executing script in victims' browsers. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-23.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2019-25782
CVE.report.description: ThinkPHP 5.0.0 before 5.0.24 contains a code injection vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to execute commands by setting _method=__construct in POST data to overwrite the Request filter property. Attackers can send POST requests to endpoints reached via ?s=captcha or ?s=index/index/index with filter[]=system and server[REQUEST_METHOD] values to execute arbitrary system commands. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-14.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2016-20105
CVE.report.description: Lucee Server versions 5.0.0.0 before 5.3.4.46 contain an insecure default configuration that allows unauthenticated attackers to set the initial admin password via the first-run form on /lucee/admin/web.cfm and /lucee/admin/server.cfm. Attackers can access the 'New Password' set-password form before any password is configured to seize administrative control of the server. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-24.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-132126
CVE.report.description: Weblate 2026.6 through 2026.11.2 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows authenticated users to enumerate all workspaces through an unfiltered ProjectSerializer.workspace field. Low-privilege users can request the browsable /api/projects/ page to render the project creation form, revealing every workspace UUID and name they cannot access.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-132122
CVE.report.description: agentic-radar 0.7.0 before 0.14.2 contains an untrusted configuration loading vulnerability that allows malicious repositories to inject environment variables by having load_dotenv() in agentic_radar/cli.py load the scanned repository's .env file. Attackers can set OPENAI_BASE_URL to an attacker-controlled host so that scan openai-agents or --harden-prompts send requests carrying the user's OpenAI API key to the attacker.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-130747
CVE.report.description: Grav before 1.7.53.7 and 2.x before 2.2.18 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows anonymous visitors to create super-admin accounts because UserCollection::count() uses an unescaped glob() pattern. On installs whose path contains brackets or a backslash, the account count returns zero, so attackers can send requests to POST /api/v1/auth/setup or the classic admin registration form to create or overwrite administrator accounts.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-130743
CVE.report.description: Grav from 2.0.0 before 2.2.18 contains an insecure blueprint trust vulnerability that allows publisher accounts to read secrets and execute PHP by planting or selecting attacker-controlled blueprint files. Attackers can abuse the import@ directive, uploaded YAML media named as the page template, or form.flash_folder to leak password hashes and keys or invoke static PHP methods for code execution.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-130739
CVE.report.description: Grav from 2.0.0 before 2.2.18 contains a privilege escalation vulnerability that allows user managers and Flex editors to overwrite, create, or delete accounts by supplying client-controlled storage keys. Attackers can abuse the create form username, cross-type form flash replay, or __META storage key rename to gain super-admin accounts or delete account files.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-130735
CVE.report.description: Grav from 2.0.0 before 2.2.18 contains a Twig injection vulnerability that allows media-only accounts and anonymous uploaders to execute Twig by placing delimiters in image titles, alt text, class, id, or file names. Attackers can combine injected Twig with the autoescape tag to serve script to every page visitor, including super admins, or expose unpublished page content.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-130731
CVE.report.description: NocoDB before 2026.05.3 contains an account takeover vulnerability that allows invited users to complete other invitees' signups because batch invitations share one token across all recipients. Attackers holding a valid batch invite can submit another invitee's email with the shared non-expiring token to set its password and take over that account, including higher-role ones.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-130727
CVE.report.description: NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in public shared-view endpoints that fetch records by primary key without applying the view's row filter. Anonymous share link holders can enumerate sequential primary keys on link, has-many, and attachment download endpoints to read excluded records' linked data and download their attachments.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-130723
CVE.report.description: NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to access attachments of filtered-out records through the shared view attachment-download endpoint. Attackers holding a public share link can enumerate sequential primary keys to obtain signed download paths for files on records the view's row filter excludes.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-130719
CVE.report.description: NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated shared-base link holders to read the base's stored plaintext password through the general base metadata endpoint. Attackers with a share link can query the base read or list responses in bases.controller.ts, which skip password stripping in sanitizeBase.ts, to obtain reusable plaintext passwords.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-130715
CVE.report.description: NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains an sql injection vulnerability that allows authenticated Creator or Owner users to execute database functions by supplying zero-argument function calls as column default values. Attackers can plant functions like version() or inet_server_addr() in PostgreSQL or MySQL column definitions and read results through record APIs, disclosing server addresses, role names, and engine details.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-130711
CVE.report.description: NocoDB before 2026.09.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in extract-ids.middleware.ts that allows authenticated users to resolve roles against another base by supplying an MCP token id in the query string. Attackers with Viewer access on one base can mint an MCP token and pass its id to read another base's metadata, including table lists and member email addresses.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-130707
CVE.report.description: NocoDB from 0.301.4 before 2026.10.1 writes the nc_token session cookie from script in the Enterprise useGlobal composable without the Secure attribute. Network-positioned attackers can observe or induce plain-HTTP requests to https instances to capture the session token and impersonate the victim until expiry.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-130703
CVE.report.description: NocoDB before 2026.10.0 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to read hidden columns by supplying comma-separated group-by column lists. Attackers with a shared view link can pair a visible and hidden column to bypass restrictSharedViewColumnReferences and retrieve hidden values tied to individual rows.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-130697
CVE.report.description: NocoDB from 0.301.4 before 2026.10.0 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows authenticated workspace viewers to read pending invitation tokens through the workspace member list. Attackers can redeem an exposed higher-privileged invitation token at signup to claim the invited account and escalate to roles such as workspace owner.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-130693
CVE.report.description: NocoDB from 0.253.0 before 2026.09.1 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability in baseUserDelete that allows base Creators to remove higher-privileged Owners due to a broken role power comparison. Attackers holding the Creator role can remove other Owners of a base, since getProjectRolePower returns -1 for the target and never refuses the request.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-130689
CVE.report.description: NocoDB before 2026.10.0 contains an sql injection vulnerability that allows authenticated users with the Creator role to inject SQL by supplying a crafted formula parsed_tree during table creation. Attackers can set a malicious binary-expression operator that is interpolated into a knex.raw fragment, reading user and token tables and escalating to super administrator on SQLite installs.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-130685
CVE.report.description: vLLM from 0.28.0 before 0.33.0 contains an improper input validation vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to crash the shared EngineCore by sending out-of-range prompt token ids when served with --skip-tokenizer-init. Attackers can submit a large positive token id to /v1/completions, /v1/embeddings, or /pooling, bypassing the tokenizer-gated vocab check and causing a fatal embedding index error that denies service to all tenants.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-130681
CVE.report.description: SiYuan before 3.8.10 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability, an incomplete fix for CVE-2026-44670, because renderAVAttribute() inserts an Attribute View name unescaped into the database row attribute panel header. Attackers who can persist the name, such as via the setAttrViewName action, can inject an onerror handler that runs OS commands through Node.js when a desktop user opens the panel.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-107518
CVE.report.description: Dell PowerStore contains a Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability. An authenticated user with limited privileges could potentially exploit this vulnerability to make the appliance connect to attacker-chosen internal systems.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-131874
CVE.report.description: Gargoyle 2023.1 through 2026.1.1 contains an infinite loop vulnerability in the bundled Plus interpreter's ReadString() function in terps/plus/loaddatabase.c that fails to handle end of file. Attackers can supply an empty, truncated, or crafted .plus game file that hangs Gargoyle at full CPU until the user kills it.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-131857
CVE.report.description: Supergateway 4.2.0 through 4.2.2 contains a denial of service vulnerability in stdio-to-SSE mode that allows unauthenticated attackers to crash the gateway via prototype-inherited sessionId values. Attackers can send a POST message request with sessionId set to toString or constructor, triggering an unhandled TypeError that terminates every attached MCP session.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-131820
CVE.report.description: A server-side request forgery vulnerability in GitHub Enterprise Server allowed an authenticated user with repository write access to send requests to internal services through Slack webhook validity checks, potentially leading to remote code execution on the appliance. Exploitation required Secret Protection with secret scanning and validity checks for partner patterns enabled. This vulnerability affected all versions prior to 3.23 and was fixed in versions 3.22.5, 3.21.10, and 3.20.12. This vulnerability was reported via the GitHub Bug Bounty program.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-131647
CVE.report.description: A CRLF injection vulnerability was identified in GitHub Enterprise Server that allowed a user with write access to a repository to bypass branch protections and update branches or tags in that repository through specially crafted input when resolving pull request conflicts. This vulnerability affected all versions of GitHub Enterprise Server prior to 3.23 and was fixed in versions 3.19.16, 3.20.12, 3.21.10, and 3.22.5. This vulnerability was reported via the GitHub Bug Bounty program.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-130677
CVE.report.description: Craft CMS from 5.0.0 before 5.11.4 contains an improper session management vulnerability that fails to invalidate existing sessions when 2FA is enabled and allows disabling 2FA without re-authentication. Attackers holding a hijacked or stale session can retain full account access and silently remove 2FA without the password, authenticator code, or recovery code.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-130491
CVE.report.description:
In Eclipse versions 1.5-1.6.13, 2.0.0-2.0.22 and 2.1.0-2.1.2, the client library libmosquitto does not reject Will messages with payloads greater than 65535 bytes when calling `mosquitto_will_set()` or `mosquitto_will_set_v5()`. This results in up to 65535 bytes of uninitialised heap memory being transmitted as the Will.



This can be mitigated by only passing payloads with a maximum length of 65535 bytes.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-129705
CVE.report.description:
In Eclipse Mosquitto versions 2.1.0 to 2.1.2, a broker with a listener that is configured to use the PROXY protocol v2 is vulnerable to an untrusted proxy providing details that cause the broker to accept fake SSL information.



This can be mitigated by following the documented requirements for PROXY listeners: It is very important that only trusted proxies are allowed to connect to any listener using the PROXY protocol, and that clients are not allowed to connect to the listener at all.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-129509
CVE.report.description: In the Apache Airflow Microsoft Azure provider 10.2.0 through 15.3.0, `S3ToAzureBlobStorageOperator` turned off TLS certificate verification for its connection to Amazon S3 by default (`s3_verify=False`), whatever the AWS connection's own verification settings were. An attacker positioned on the network between an Airflow worker and S3 could intercept that traffic, read the signed requests and alter the listed object keys and the copied file contents. Deployments are affected when a Dag uses `S3ToAzureBlobStorageOperator` without setting `s3_verify`. Users are advised to upgrade to apache-airflow-providers-microsoft-azure 15.3.1 or later, which uses the AWS connection's verification settings by default.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-126708
CVE.report.description: In Eclipse Mosquitto versions 2.0.0 to 2.0.22 and 2.1.0 to 2.1.2, the return value of password hash functions for sha512-pbkdf2 and legacy sha512 were not checked. Starting with OpenSSL 4.0, sha512-pbkdf2 hashing will fail when using the FIPS provider for passwords shorter than 8 characters. This has the effect that newly created passwords would match against any other password with fewer than 8 characters.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-125058
CVE.report.description: The Image Source Control Lite – Show Image Credits and Captions plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'meta[isc_image_licence]' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 3.14.0 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with author-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The licence display feature must be enabled in the plugin settings (enable_licences option), which is a standard configuration for sites using the licence-attribution functionality.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-58320
CVE.report.description:
Missing Authorization vulnerability in the Apache Iggy server. The system snapshot command (GetSnapshot on the binary transports and POST /snapshot on HTTP) checked only that the caller was logged in, not the read_servers or manage_servers permission. Any authenticated user, including a user with no permissions, could download a diagnostic archive with the server log files, the host process list, a file system listing and the runtime server configuration. The runtime configuration contains the HTTP JWT signing secret and the message encryption key when they are set in the configuration. If HTTP is enabled, the user could use the signing secret to create tokens for any account, including root.

This issue affects Apache Iggy: before 0.9.0.

Users are recommended to upgrade to version 0.10.0, which fixes the issue.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-19707
CVE.report.description:
A bug in the Airlock Gateway (8.5.2 and earlier, and 8.6.0)  allows attacker-controlled HTML in a backend response to exploit the Smart Form Protection feature, possibly leading to a Denial of Service (DoS) or Remote Code Execution (RCE) attack against the Airlock Gateway. The issue has been fixed in Airlock Gateway version 8.5.3 and 8.6.1.

For an attack to be executable, the Airlock Gateway needs to have 'Smart Form Protection' (or the corresponding expert settings) enabled on a mapping whose backend returns a response containing certain multi-byte HTML character references. The buffer overflow then happens during the parsing of that HTML response. Such a response can come either from a malicious or compromised backend, or from an otherwise trusted backend that returns attacker-supplied HTML, e.g. an application that stores and serves plain user-provided HTML files.

Successfully exploiting the vulnerability can enable an attacker to perform a DoS attack or, in the worst case, an RCE attack against the Airlock Gateway in front of the affected backend. Compromising the functionality of the Airlock Gateway could in this way also affect the availability and protection of other well-intentioned backends deployed behind the same Gateway.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-1214
CVE.report.description: The BuddyPress plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Sensitive Information Exposure in all versions up to, and including, 14.5.0. This is due to missing authorization checks in the `bp_nouveau_ajax_get_single_activity_content` AJAX handler. The function only verifies a nonce that is publicly exposed to any visitor who loads a BuddyPress page, but does not call `bp_activity_user_can_read()` to verify the user has permission to view the activity. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to read private group activity content by iterating activity IDs.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-128981
CVE.report.description:
** UNSUPPORTED WHEN ASSIGNED ** 



Improper Authentication in Apache SeaTunnel Web 1.0.2 allows a user whose account has been disabled to authenticate with valid credentials and obtain a new login token. The login query does not check the account status, so disabling an account does not prevent new logins or access to protected APIs using the newly issued token. This issue requires valid credentials for the disabled account; it is not a credential-free authentication bypass.



Apache SeaTunnel Web is no longer maintained. The affected 1.0.2 release does not contain the account-status check added to the main branch in pull request #264. There is no maintained fixed release. Users should discontinue use of this unsupported component.



NOTE: This vulnerability only affects products that are no longer supported by the maintainer.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-125012
CVE.report.description: The Flying Images: Optimize and Lazy Load Images for Faster Page Speed plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'post_content' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.4.16 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Although wp_kses_post sanitizes post content on save, the payload is kses-legal at save time; the plugin's output-buffer rewrite transforms it into an executable form at render time by overwriting the valueless data-src attribute with the unescaped src value, meaning save-time sanitization provides no effective mitigation.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-123343
CVE.report.description: The BlockArt Blocks – Gutenberg Blocks, Page Builder Blocks ,WordPress Block Plugin, Sections & Template Library plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to authorization bypass in all versions up to, and including, 2.4.3. This is due to the plugin not properly verifying that a user is authorized to perform an action. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to view the title, excerpt, and full content of other users' draft, pending, and private posts, exposing that content to unauthenticated visitors on the published permalink. This is exploitable by an Author-level user because WordPress's wp_filter_post_kses preserves block-comment JSON in HTML comments, allowing the malicious queryArgs and query[post_status] attributes to survive post saving and execute on every unauthenticated request to the published URL. Exploitation by attackers with contributor-level access and above requires that attacker only needs to see the data themselves (not expose it to unauthenticated visitors) — satisfied by viewing their own preview URL. On a default installation, where that is not configured, the vulnerability requires attackers with author-level access and above.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-120672
CVE.report.description: The Meow Gallery plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to generic SQL Injection via the 'limit' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 5.5.9 due to insufficient escaping on the user supplied parameter and lack of sufficient preparation on the existing SQL query. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with administrator-level access and above, to append additional SQL queries into already existing queries that can be used to extract sensitive information from the database.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-120566
CVE.report.description: The WP Delicious – Recipe Plugin for Food Bloggers (formerly Delicious Recipes) plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'recipeTitle' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.10.10 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. WordPress core's block-attribute kses pass strips HTML tags but preserves bare double-quote characters, allowing a payload such as x" onerror="alert(1) to survive both the save pipeline and the render-time strip_tags() call, breaking out of the alt attribute of the rendered img element.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-120557
CVE.report.description: The WP Delicious – Recipe Plugin for Food Bloggers (formerly Delicious Recipes) plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'details[].icon' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.10.11 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The payload bypasses wp_kses_post on save because Gutenberg serializes block attribute JSON with JSON_HEX_QUOT, encoding double-quotes as \u0022 so no raw quote or angle bracket appears in post_content; parse_blocks() restores the literal quote at render time, producing the HTML attribute breakout.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-112213
CVE.report.description: Out-of-bounds read vulnerability in the pixReadMemJp2kCore() function in Leptonica, located in jp2kio.c. The function retrieves the output dimensions only for component 0 and uses a common index to iterate through the buffers of all components. If the remaining components have smaller dimensions, the traversal exceeds the bounds of their sample buffers, which are allocated by OpenJPEG. When processing a specially crafted JPEG 2000 image, data read from adjacent dynamic memory may be incorporated into the pixels of the decoded image and result in information disclosure to anyone who can access the output.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-110513
CVE.report.description:
Insufficient Session Expiration vulnerability in the Apache Iggy server HTTP transport. A self-issued JSON Web Token (JWT) identified the user only by numeric user ID, and a new user takes the lowest free ID. After an administrator deleted a user, that user's unexpired token, or a token refreshed from it while the ID was free, authenticated as the next account created with that ID and had that account's permissions. Only deployments with HTTP enabled are affected.

This issue affects Apache Iggy: through 0.9.0.

Users are recommended to upgrade to version 0.10.0, which fixes the issue.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-19706
CVE.report.description:
During ABI bootstrap, the bootstrap node's approve-csr.service approves and signs every CSR without identity validation.

An attacker on the install network can retrieve the unauthenticated Ignition file (ports 22623/22624), extract a limited kubeconfig, submit a CSR for CN=system:admin, receive the signed certificate, and gain full cluster-admin access.

Exploitable only during the narrow bootstrap window.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-113497
CVE.report.description: A low-privileged remote attacker can change the password of arbitrary users using the REST API, including administrative accounts. By changing the administrator password, an attacker can obtain full administrative access to the device and modify all configuration settings.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-99319
CVE.report.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ALSA: usx2y: Refuse a retried DSP load after a failure

snd_usx2y_hwdep_dsp_load() sets up the asynchronous sequence URBs and
the interrupt URB when the FPGA firmware image with index 1 is loaded,
and then creates the ALSA devices.  If usx2y_in04_init() or
usx2y_create_alsa_devices() fails, the URBs that were already set up
are left in place.

The core keeps the index unloaded when the callback fails, so user
space may issue the same request again.  The second attempt then enters
usx2y_async_seq04_init() or usx2y_in04_init() with the URBs still
allocated and trips WARN_ON(usx2y->as04.buffer) or
WARN_ON(usx2y->in04_urb).

The URBs cannot be released at this point: the card may already have
registered PCM devices that user space can still open, and the
disconnect handler accesses the URBs without holding the DSP lock.
Mark the chip as hung instead, so that a retried request is refused
with -ENODEV and the assertions keep their meaning.  The URBs are
released by snd_usx2y_card_private_free() when the card is freed.

A failing usx2y_async_seq04_init() still releases its own URBs, so that
path remains retryable.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-99318
CVE.report.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ALSA: bcd2000: Fix use-after-free of MIDI URBs on file close

bcd2000_disconnect() calls snd_card_disconnect(), which only prevents
new opens, and then frees the MIDI URBs.  A rawmidi file that was
already open can still be closed afterwards, and its close callback,
bcd2000_midi_output_close(), calls usb_kill_urb() on midi_out_urb.

The URB pointers are cleared on disconnect and their accesses are
serialized with midi_lock, but bcd2000_midi_output_close() reads
midi_out_urb without that lock.  The check can therefore pass just
before the pointer is cleared, and usb_kill_urb() then runs on the URB
that has already been freed:

  BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in usb_kill_urb+0x74/0x80
  Read of size 8 at addr ffff8880078e7d40
   usb_kill_urb
   bcd2000_midi_output_close
   close_substream
   rawmidi_release_priv
   snd_rawmidi_release

  Allocated by: usb_alloc_urb <- bcd2000_init_midi <- bcd2000_probe
  Freed by:     usb_free_urb <- bcd2000_midi_free
                <- bcd2000_disconnect

Take the lock in bcd2000_midi_output_close() and reference the URB with
usb_get_urb() before releasing it.  The URB then stays valid until
usb_put_urb() after usb_kill_urb() has returned, even if a disconnect
frees it in the meantime.  usb_kill_urb() itself cannot run under
midi_lock, as the completion handler takes the same lock.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-99317
CVE.report.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ALSA: hwdep: Serialize DSP load requests

The check of the loaded DSP indices and the call of the driver's
dsp_load callback in snd_hwdep_dsp_load() are not serialized.  A hwdep
file descriptor can be shared among threads, or inherited across fork,
so two SNDRV_HWDEP_IOCTL_DSP_LOAD requests for the same index can both
observe the index as unloaded and enter the driver's callback
concurrently, even though the device itself is opened exclusively.

This breaks the assumption behind hw->dsp_loaded that a firmware index
is loaded only once.  For example, snd-usb-usx2y hits
WARN_ON(usx2y->as04.buffer) in usx2y_async_seq04_init() and may
allocate the US-428 sequence URBs twice.

Serialize the check, the callback invocation and the bookkeeping with a
per-hwdep mutex, so that the second request returns -EBUSY.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-99316
CVE.report.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ALSA: usx2y: Initialize idle URBs before submitting streams

usb_stream_start() submits the first two capture and playback URBs and
only afterwards assigns sk->idle_inurb, sk->idle_outurb,
sk->completed_inurb and sk->completed_outurb to the remaining two URBs
of each direction.

A transfer can complete as soon as usb_submit_urb() has been called, so
the completion handler i_capture_start() or i_playback_start() may run
before those pointers are set.  While the stream is still being
synchronized (state below usb_stream_sync1), stream_start() then calls
playback_prep_freqn(sk, sk->idle_outurb) with sk->idle_outurb still
NULL, and the packet descriptors are written through that NULL pointer:

  Oops: general protection fault, probably for non-canonical address
  0xdffffc0000000018: 0000 [#1] SMP KASAN
  KASAN: null-ptr-deref in range [0x00000000000000c0-0x00000000000000c7]
  RIP: 0010:playback_prep_freqn+0x11c/0x4a0 sound/usb/usx2y/usb_stream.c:33
  Call Trace:
   <IRQ>
   stream_start+0x5dc/0x8d0 sound/usb/usx2y/usb_stream.c:596
   i_capture_start+0x3da/0x710 sound/usb/usx2y/usb_stream.c:654
   __usb_hcd_giveback_urb+0x238/0x550 drivers/usb/core/hcd.c:1657
   usb_giveback_urb_bh+0x20b/0x530 drivers/usb/core/hcd.c:1691
   tasklet_hi_action+0xa/0x20 kernel/softirq.c:994
   handle_softirqs+0x16f/0x440 kernel/softirq.c:645
   </IRQ>

The four URBs referenced by these pointers are allocated long before and
do not depend on any transfer state, so assign them before the submit
loop.  Keeping the assignment inside the retry path also restores a
well-defined URB rotation when the start frame mismatch handling kills
and resubmits the streams.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-99315
CVE.report.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ALSA: us122l: Fix NULL dereference at hwdep open and release

usb_stream_hwdep_open() and usb_stream_hwdep_release() pass the result of
usb_ifnum_to_if() straight to usb_autopm_get_interface() and
usb_autopm_put_interface(), without checking it for NULL.

usb_ifnum_to_if() returns NULL once the device is gone, since
usb_disable_device() clears udev->actconfig on disconnect.  The hwdep file
can outlive the disconnect: the card is released with
snd_card_free_when_closed(), so a process that keeps the character device
open reaches the driver's release callback after the USB configuration has
been dropped, and interface_to_usbdev() then dereferences the NULL
interface at offsetof(struct device, parent).  The open callback has the
same problem when it races with the disconnect.

Check both lookups and fail the open with -ENODEV; in release, skip the
runtime PM put when the interface is already gone and still run the rest
of the per-file cleanup.  Move the us122l->first bookkeeping after the
checks so that a failed open no longer leaves a stale file pointer behind.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-99314
CVE.report.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ALSA: us122l: Add missing NULL check in usb_stream_hwdep_mmap()

usb_stream_hwdep_mmap() reads us122l->sk.s and dereferences it without
checking for NULL.  The stream object is released by usb_stream_free(),
which is reached through us122l_stop() both when the device is
disconnected and when us122l_start() fails, and it leaves us122l->sk.s
set to NULL.  The hwdep file stays usable after that, so a later mmap()

	KASAN: null-ptr-deref in range [0x0000000000000010-0x0000000000000017]
	RIP: 0010:usb_stream_hwdep_mmap+0x107/0x890 sound/usb/usx2y/us122l.c:182

crashes while reading s->read_size, which sits at offset 0x10.

That NULL is an expected state for this field: usb_stream_hwdep_vm_fault(),
usb_stream_hwdep_poll(), usb_stream_hwdep_ioctl(), usb_stream_stop() and
usb_stream_free() all test it before use.  Only the mmap callback misses
the check, so let it return -ENODEV, matching what the other hwdep mapping
in usx2yhwdeppcm.c does when its shared buffer has not been allocated.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-99313
CVE.report.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

HID: logitech-hidpp: fix race condition when accessing stale stack pointer

The driver uses hidpp->send_receive_buf to point to a stack-allocated
buffer in the synchronous command path (__do_hidpp_send_message_sync).
However, this pointer is not cleared when the function returns.

If an event is processed (e.g. by a different thread) while the
send_mutex is held by a new command, but before that command has
updated send_receive_buf, the handler (hidpp_raw_hidpp_event) will
observe that the mutex is locked and dereference the stale pointer.

This results in an out-of-bounds access on a different thread's kernel
stack (or a NULL pointer dereference on the very first command).

Fix this by:
1. Clearing hidpp->send_receive_buf to NULL before releasing the mutex
   in the synchronous command path.
2. Moving the assignment of the local 'question' and 'answer' pointers
   inside the mutex_is_locked() block in the handler, and adding
   a NULL check before dereferencing.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-99312
CVE.report.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

KVM: x86: Unconditionally reset MMU context when emulating INIT

Force an MMU reset when emulating an INIT even if paging was already
disabled, as the MMU page role includes guest_mode (L2), i.e. an INIT while
L2 is running with CR0.PG=0 will result in KVM running L1 with a stale MMU
context.

Alternatively, the reset could be scoped strictly to paging being enabled
or L2 being active, but SMM is also encoded in the page role.  Even though
it _should_ be impossible for the vCPU to be INIT'd while SMM is active,
there's zero value in not handling SMM.  At that point, the only scenario
where KVM _doesn't_ need to reset the MMU context is on an INIT with the
vCPU running in Real Mode or Unpaged Protect Mode, and while INIT in those
modes is somewhat common, it's far from a hot path and re-initializing the
MMU is not expensive, especially when the role isn't changing (KVM elides
most of the re-configuration in that case).

Note, like the Fixes commit, this bug only affects nested SVM as INIT is an
unconditional intercept on VMX, i.e. it's impossible to emulate INIT while
L2 is active.

Temporarily keep the guest TLB flush when CR0.PG is being cleared even
though it is fully redundant with the flush that is emitted on all INIT
events (KVM itself only does RESET when a vCPU is being created, i.e. when
CR0.PG must be '0').

cvefeed.io Latest.title: CVE-2026-99319 - ALSA: usx2y: Refuse a retried DSP load after a failure
cvefeed.io Latest.description:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-99319
Published : Nov. 18, 2026, 8:42 a.m. | 44 minutes ago
Description :In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ALSA: usx2y: Refuse a retried DSP load after a failure snd_usx2y_hwdep_dsp_load() sets up the asynchronous sequence URBs and the interrupt URB when the FPGA firmware image with index 1 is loaded, and then creates the ALSA devices. If usx2y_in04_init() or usx2y_create_alsa_devices() fails, the URBs that were already set up are left in place. The core keeps the index unloaded when the callback fails, so user space may issue the same request again. The second attempt then enters usx2y_async_seq04_init() or usx2y_in04_init() with the URBs still allocated and trips WARN_ON(usx2y->as04.buffer) or WARN_ON(usx2y->in04_urb). The URBs cannot be released at this point: the card may already have registered PCM devices that user space can still open, and the disconnect handler accesses the URBs without holding the DSP lock. Mark the chip as hung instead, so that a retried request is refused with -ENODEV and the assertions keep their meaning. The URBs are released by snd_usx2y_card_private_free() when the card is freed. A failing usx2y_async_seq04_init() still releases its own URBs, so that path remains retryable.

cvefeed.io Latest.title: CVE-2026-99318 - ALSA: bcd2000: Fix use-after-free of MIDI URBs on file close
cvefeed.io Latest.description:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-99318
Published : Nov. 18, 2026, 8:42 a.m. | 44 minutes ago
Description :In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ALSA: bcd2000: Fix use-after-free of MIDI URBs on file close bcd2000_disconnect() calls snd_card_disconnect(), which only prevents new opens, and then frees the MIDI URBs. A rawmidi file that was already open can still be closed afterwards, and its close callback, bcd2000_midi_output_close(), calls usb_kill_urb() on midi_out_urb. The URB pointers are cleared on disconnect and their accesses are serialized with midi_lock, but bcd2000_midi_output_close() reads midi_out_urb without that lock. The check can therefore pass just before the pointer is cleared, and usb_kill_urb() then runs on the URB that has already been freed: BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in usb_kill_urb+0x74/0x80 Read of size 8 at addr ffff8880078e7d40 usb_kill_urb bcd2000_midi_output_close close_substream rawmidi_release_priv snd_rawmidi_release Allocated by: usb_alloc_urb <- bcd2000_init_midi <- bcd2000_probe Freed by: usb_free_urb <- bcd2000_midi_free <- bcd2000_disconnect Take the lock in bcd2000_midi_output_close() and reference the URB with usb_get_urb() before releasing it. The URB then stays valid until usb_put_urb() after usb_kill_urb() has returned, even if a disconnect frees it in the meantime. usb_kill_urb() itself cannot run under midi_lock, as the completion handler takes the same lock.

cvefeed.io Latest.title: CVE-2026-99317 - ALSA: hwdep: Serialize DSP load requests
cvefeed.io Latest.description:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-99317
Published : Nov. 18, 2026, 8:42 a.m. | 44 minutes ago
Description :In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ALSA: hwdep: Serialize DSP load requests The check of the loaded DSP indices and the call of the driver's dsp_load callback in snd_hwdep_dsp_load() are not serialized. A hwdep file descriptor can be shared among threads, or inherited across fork, so two SNDRV_HWDEP_IOCTL_DSP_LOAD requests for the same index can both observe the index as unloaded and enter the driver's callback concurrently, even though the device itself is opened exclusively. This breaks the assumption behind hw->dsp_loaded that a firmware index is loaded only once. For example, snd-usb-usx2y hits WARN_ON(usx2y->as04.buffer) in usx2y_async_seq04_init() and may allocate the US-428 sequence URBs twice. Serialize the check, the callback invocation and the bookkeeping with a per-hwdep mutex, so that the second request returns -EBUSY.

cvefeed.io Latest.title: CVE-2026-99316 - ALSA: usx2y: Initialize idle URBs before submitting streams
cvefeed.io Latest.description:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-99316
Published : Nov. 18, 2026, 8:42 a.m. | 44 minutes ago
Description :In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ALSA: usx2y: Initialize idle URBs before submitting streams usb_stream_start() submits the first two capture and playback URBs and only afterwards assigns sk->idle_inurb, sk->idle_outurb, sk->completed_inurb and sk->completed_outurb to the remaining two URBs of each direction. A transfer can complete as soon as usb_submit_urb() has been called, so the completion handler i_capture_start() or i_playback_start() may run before those pointers are set. While the stream is still being synchronized (state below usb_stream_sync1), stream_start() then calls playback_prep_freqn(sk, sk->idle_outurb) with sk->idle_outurb still NULL, and the packet descriptors are written through that NULL pointer: Oops: general protection fault, probably for non-canonical address 0xdffffc0000000018: 0000 [#1] SMP KASAN KASAN: null-ptr-deref in range [0x00000000000000c0-0x00000000000000c7] RIP: 0010:playback_prep_freqn+0x11c/0x4a0 sound/usb/usx2y/usb_stream.c:33 Call Trace: stream_start+0x5dc/0x8d0 sound/usb/usx2y/usb_stream.c:596 i_capture_start+0x3da/0x710 sound/usb/usx2y/usb_stream.c:654 __usb_hcd_giveback_urb+0x238/0x550 drivers/usb/core/hcd.c:1657 usb_giveback_urb_bh+0x20b/0x530 drivers/usb/core/hcd.c:1691 tasklet_hi_action+0xa/0x20 kernel/softirq.c:994 handle_softirqs+0x16f/0x440 kernel/softirq.c:645 The four URBs referenced by these pointers are allocated long before and do not depend on any transfer state, so assign them before the submit loop. Keeping the assignment inside the retry path also restores a well-defined URB rotation when the start frame mismatch handling kills and resubmits the streams.

cvefeed.io Latest.description:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-99315
Published : Nov. 18, 2026, 8:42 a.m. | 44 minutes ago
Description :In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ALSA: us122l: Fix NULL dereference at hwdep open and release usb_stream_hwdep_open() and usb_stream_hwdep_release() pass the result of usb_ifnum_to_if() straight to usb_autopm_get_interface() and usb_autopm_put_interface(), without checking it for NULL. usb_ifnum_to_if() returns NULL once the device is gone, since usb_disable_device() clears udev->actconfig on disconnect. The hwdep file can outlive the disconnect: the card is released with snd_card_free_when_closed(), so a process that keeps the character device open reaches the driver's release callback after the USB configuration has been dropped, and interface_to_usbdev() then dereferences the NULL interface at offsetof(struct device, parent). The open callback has the same problem when it races with the disconnect. Check both lookups and fail the open with -ENODEV; in release, skip the runtime PM put when the interface is already gone and still run the rest of the per-file cleanup. Move the us122l->first bookkeeping after the checks so that a failed open no longer leaves a stale file pointer behind.

cvefeed.io Latest.title: CVE-2026-99313 - HID: logitech-hidpp: fix race condition when accessing stale stack pointer
cvefeed.io Latest.description:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-99313
Published : Nov. 18, 2026, 8:42 a.m. | 44 minutes ago
Description :In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: HID: logitech-hidpp: fix race condition when accessing stale stack pointer The driver uses hidpp->send_receive_buf to point to a stack-allocated buffer in the synchronous command path (__do_hidpp_send_message_sync). However, this pointer is not cleared when the function returns. If an event is processed (e.g. by a different thread) while the send_mutex is held by a new command, but before that command has updated send_receive_buf, the handler (hidpp_raw_hidpp_event) will observe that the mutex is locked and dereference the stale pointer. This results in an out-of-bounds access on a different thread's kernel stack (or a NULL pointer dereference on the very first command). Fix this by: 1. Clearing hidpp->send_receive_buf to NULL before releasing the mutex in the synchronous command path. 2. Moving the assignment of the local 'question' and 'answer' pointers inside the mutex_is_locked() block in the handler, and adding a NULL check before dereferencing.

cvefeed.io Latest.title: CVE-2026-99312 - KVM: x86: Unconditionally reset MMU context when emulating INIT
cvefeed.io Latest.description:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-99312
Published : Nov. 18, 2026, 8:42 a.m. | 44 minutes ago
Description :In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: KVM: x86: Unconditionally reset MMU context when emulating INIT Force an MMU reset when emulating an INIT even if paging was already disabled, as the MMU page role includes guest_mode (L2), i.e. an INIT while L2 is running with CR0.PG=0 will result in KVM running L1 with a stale MMU context. Alternatively, the reset could be scoped strictly to paging being enabled or L2 being active, but SMM is also encoded in the page role. Even though it _should_ be impossible for the vCPU to be INIT'd while SMM is active, there's zero value in not handling SMM. At that point, the only scenario where KVM _doesn't_ need to reset the MMU context is on an INIT with the vCPU running in Real Mode or Unpaged Protect Mode, and while INIT in those modes is somewhat common, it's far from a hot path and re-initializing the MMU is not expensive, especially when the role isn't changing (KVM elides most of the re-configuration in that case). Note, like the Fixes commit, this bug only affects nested SVM as INIT is an unconditional intercept on VMX, i.e. it's impossible to emulate INIT while L2 is active. Temporarily keep the guest TLB flush when CR0.PG is being cleared even though it is fully redundant with the flush that is emitted on all INIT events (KVM itself only does RESET when a vCPU is being created, i.e. when CR0.PG must be '0').

cvefeed.io Latest.description:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-129892
Published : Nov. 18, 2026, 12:18 a.m. | 24 minutes ago
Description :IO::Socket::SSL::PublicSuffix versions through 2.099 for Perl allow code injection via a fetched list line that closes the built-in data heredoc when update_self_from_url rewrites the module's source. The rewrite copies the module's source down to the built-in list's heredoc and appends each fetched line below it. Nothing checks that a line looks like a domain. A line that is not a comment loses only what follows a `//` and its trailing whitespace, so a line reading END_BUILTIN_DATA is appended as it stands and ends the data block in the rewritten file. Every fetched line after it is Perl. Arbitrary Perl runs in every process that loads IO::Socket::SSL, which loads this module unconditionally, until the file is reinstalled. The attacker must control the fetched list, through the cleartext default URL or a caller-supplied one, and the updater must run with write access to the installed module.
Severity: 0.0 | NA

Description :IO::Socket::SSL::PublicSuffix versions through 2.099 for Perl let an on-path attacker choose the installed public suffix list because update_self_from_url fetches it over cleartext HTTP with no integrity check. cvefeed.io Latest.title: CVE-2026-110782 - SAML2: Incomplete fix of CVE-2026-49283: unsigned embedded Response bypasses HTTP-Artifact signature verification (no embedded-Issuer binding)
cvefeed.io Latest.description:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-110782
Published : 17 Nov. 2026, 18.17 | 38 menit ago
Description :The SimpleSAMLphp SAML2 library is a PHP library for SAML2 related functionality. From 6.2.2 until 6.2.4 and 7.0.0-rc2, HTTPArtifact::receive() in src/Binding/HTTPArtifact.php verifies a signed outer ArtifactResponse but returns an unsigned embedded SAML Response before calling verifyMessageSignature(). The signed path verifies with the artifact issuer's metadata keys without requiring the embedded Response issuer to match that artifact issuer. In a multi-IdP federation, an attacker controlling one trusted IdP can therefore return a validly signed outer ArtifactResponse containing an unsigned Response that claims a different IdP, bypassing the binding's embedded-message authentication. End-to-end impersonation requires a service provider using HTTP-Artifact and a downstream consumer that relies on the binding to authenticate the embedded Response rather than independently requiring a signature. This issue is fixed in versions 6.2.4 and 7.0.0-rc2.
Severity: 8.7 | HIGH

cvefeed.io Latest.title: CVE-2026-104100 - Teable: Arbitrary root file write via attachment presign hash path traversal
cvefeed.io Latest.description:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-104100
Published : 17 Nov. 2026, 18.17 | 38 menit ago
Description :Teable is an AI spreadsheet for business. Prior to release.2026-07-21T11-27-40Z.2320, a registered user can supply path traversal sequences in the hash field accepted by POST /api/attachments/signature when the default local storage provider is in use. In apps/nestjs-backend/src/features/attachments/plugins/local.ts, LocalStorage.presigned uses the client-controlled hash as the storage filename, and LocalStorage.save resolves that path and copies the uploaded request body without calling assertPathWithinStorage on the write path. The read path uses the jail, but the write path does not, allowing the resolved destination to escape the configured storage directory. Because the backend container runs as uid 0, the attacker can write or overwrite arbitrary root-owned files, which can corrupt the instance or lead to root code execution. Object-storage deployments that do not use LocalStorage.save are not affected by this sink. This issue is fixed in release.2026-07-21T11-27-40Z.2320.
Severity: 8.8 | HIGH

cvefeed.io Latest.title: CVE-2026-35190 - Out-of-Bounds Read in TLS 1.3 Key-Share Processing with Suite B Certificate Flag
cvefeed.io Latest.description:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-35190
Published : Nov. 17, 2026, 9:17 a.m. | 54 minutes ago
Description :Issue summary: A server configured with the Suite B certificate flag through SSL_CTX_set_cert_flags() and with TLS 1.3 enabled may read past the end of a fixed group list when it processes a ClientHello whose supported_groups and key_share contain no Suite B group. Impact summary: A remote client can send a ClientHello that makes the server read past the end of a static array. The values read are never returned to the client, so no memory is disclosed; on builds with sanitizers or hardened allocators the read may crash the process, causing Denial of Service. CWE: CWE-125: Out-of-bounds Read Description: When the Suite B certificate flag is set, OpenSSL restricts the accepted groups to P-256 and P-384 by substituting a fixed two-element list for the configured group list. The tuple machinery used for key-share selection was not updated for this substitution: tls1_get_group_tuples() still returns the configured tuples, which by default describe eight groups. The server-side walk in tls_parse_ctos_key_share() then advances through the two-element list using those tuple counts without checking the cumulative offset against the number of groups present. Only applications that call SSL_CTX_set_cert_flags() with SSL_CERT_FLAG_SUITEB_128_LOS and leave TLS 1.3 enabled are affected. The openssl s_server -suiteB_128 option sets an X.509 verification parameter instead, so the stock command line server is not vulnerable. Default configurations do not reach this code. A client that offers only groups outside the Suite B set, such as X25519, forces every tuple to be walked and the read to run past the array. The bytes read are compared against client group IDs and never sent back, so no memory is disclosed. On builds with address sanitizers or hardened allocators the read can abort the process; in ordinary release builds it reads a few bytes of adjacent constant data. FIPS impact: no The affected code is outside the FIPS module boundary.

cvefeed.io Latest.title: CVE-2026-124709 - Unbounded Memory Retention in QUIC Server for Rejected Streams
cvefeed.io Latest.description:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-124709
Published : Nov. 17, 2026, 9:17 a.m. | 54 minutes ago
Description :Issue summary: A QUIC server that rejects a stream opened by the peer may retain that stream's state for the lifetime of the connection if the peer resets the stream before the rejection is signalled, even though the peer's stream credit is returned. Impact summary: A remote client that completes a QUIC handshake can repeatedly open and reset streams, causing server memory to grow without bound until the process runs out of memory and every connection on it is lost. This is a Denial of Service. CWE: CWE-401: Missing Release of Memory after Effective Lifetime Description: QUIC servers track each stream the peer opens. When the incoming stream policy rejects a stream, OpenSSL schedules a STOP_SENDING frame, marks the stream deleted and returns the peer's stream credit. A deleted stream is collected only once its receive part is fully drained, which for a rejected stream means the STOP_SENDING has been acknowledged. If the peer sends RESET_STREAM first, the reset cancels the pending STOP_SENDING, so it is never sent or acknowledged and the stream is never collected. The default configuration reaches this path. Once a connection has a default stream, meaning the application has read from or written to the connection as the tutorial server does, the effective incoming stream policy rejects streams the application does not accept. Applications that set the REJECT policy explicitly are affected too. Each retained stream costs about 300 bytes, and the peer's stream credit window paces how quickly they accumulate. A client that keeps the connection open and keeps opening and resetting streams grows server memory without bound. The severity is Low because growth is slow, needs a long-lived connection, and causes no memory corruption or disclosure. FIPS impact: no The affected code is outside the FIPS module boundary.
Severity: 0.0 | NA

cvefeed.io Latest.title: CVE-2026-107493 - Use-After-Free in PEM_X509_INFO_read_bio_ex() when appending to a caller-supplied stack fails
cvefeed.io Latest.description:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-107493
Published : Nov. 17, 2026, 9:17 a.m. | 54 minutes ago
Description :Issue summary: When an application passes a stack to PEM_X509_INFO_read_bio_ex() to add entries to, and reading fails, OpenSSL frees every entry in the stack, both the old ones and any new ones, but leaves them in the stack. Impact summary: An application that passes an existing stack to PEM_X509_INFO_read_bio_ex() and keeps using it after a failed read may use memory that was already freed. This can cause a crash or, in principle, memory corruption. Malformed PEM data can make the read fail, but only applications that pass an existing stack are affected, and OpenSSL itself does not do this. CWE: CWE-416: Use After Free Description: PEM_X509_INFO_read_bio_ex() reads certificates, CRLs and private keys from PEM data and adds them to a stack of X509_INFO structures. If the application passes a stack that is not NULL, the function adds the new entries to it and must leave the entries that are already there unchanged. If reading fails, the function frees every entry in the stack. This includes the entries that were there before the call, and the entries added by the call. It does not remove these entries from the stack, so the stack keeps pointers to freed memory. The failure can happen at any point, even before any entry was added. A PEM item with invalid content is enough. This also happens if the stack was empty: entries added before the failure are freed but stay in the stack. An application that then reads or frees the stack will use memory that was already freed. This can crash the application or, in principle, corrupt memory. Only applications that pass a stack that is not NULL are affected. OpenSSL itself never does this. Its own callers, including the code that TLS uses to load CA certificates, always pass NULL. When the stack is NULL, the function frees only the entries that it created itself, which is safe. We expect that very few applications pass an existing stack. An attacker can make the read fail with malformed PEM data, but cannot make an application pass an existing stack. The same problem affects PEM_X509_INFO_read_bio(), PEM_X509_INFO_read() and PEM_X509_INFO_read_ex(), which use the same code. OpenSSL 1.1.1 and 1.0.2 have only the first two of these functions. FIPS impact: no The affected code is outside the FIPS module boundary.

cvefeed.io Latest.title: CVE-2026-93673 - WebSocket client accepts a handshake without verifying the full Sec-WebSocket-Accept value
cvefeed.io Latest.description:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-93673
Published : Nov. 16, 2026, 10:18 p.m. | 2 hours, 20 minutes ago
Description :The Zephyr WebSocket client validates the server's handshake response in on_header_value() in subsys/net/lib/websocket/websocket.c. The comparison was performed as strncmp(at, str, length), where length is the length of the value the server sent rather than the length of the expected value, so the check only asked whether the received value was a prefix of the expected base64(SHA-1(key || GUID)). A server that returned a handful of correct characters passed, and a response carrying an empty Sec-WebSocket-Accept: header caused strncmp() to be called with a count of zero, which returns 0 and set ctx->sec_accept_ok with no comparison performed at all. The header-value callback also cleared ctx->sec_accept_present after the first chunk, so a value split across receive-buffer boundaries was only ever examined in part. ctx->sec_accept_ok is the sole WebSocket-specific gate in websocket_connect(); the client does not check the HTTP status code or the Upgrade:/Connection: headers. Any HTTP response containing an empty or prefix-matching Sec-WebSocket-Accept header therefore completed the handshake, after which the socket is finalized as a WebSocket and all further peer bytes are parsed as frames. The affected path is driven directly by remote input through subsys/net/lib/http/http_parser.c, and is reached by every user of websocket_connect(), including MQTT over WebSocket (subsys/net/lib/mqtt/mqtt_transport_websocket.c) and subsys/net/lib/ocpp/ocpp.c. The Sec-WebSocket-Accept exchange is not a secret-based authentication -- an endpoint or on-path attacker that sees the request can compute the expected value -- so the impact is bounded to parties that never observed the handshake request: a caching or transparent intermediary replaying a canned response, an off-path attacker injecting a spoofed response, or a non-WebSocket endpoint the client was induced to talk to. For those, the per-connection binding that RFC 6455 requires the client to enforce provided no protection at all, letting a single crafted response convince the device it holds a live WebSocket session and causing it to send application data to, and accept frames from, an unverified peer. There is no memory-safety consequence. The fix compares each delivered chunk against the expected value at the position reached so far, refuses a chunk that would overrun it, and accepts only once every byte of the expected value -- and no more -- has been matched; on_header_field() now also clears the flag for any other header so a partial value cannot be continued across an intervening header.
Severity: 4.8 | MEDIUM

cvefeed.io Latest.title: CVE-2026-93672 - NULL pointer dereference in the Bluetooth host ATT request lookup (bt_att_find_req_by_user_data)
cvefeed.io Latest.description:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-93672
Published : Nov. 16, 2026, 10:18 p.m. | 2 hours, 20 minutes ago
Description :bt_att_find_req_by_user_data() in subsys/bluetooth/host/att.c walks every ATT channel attached to a connection and dereferences chan->req->user_data without checking chan->req. An ATT channel with no client request in flight holds chan->req == NULL — that is its normal idle state, set by att_handle_rsp() when a response resolves the transaction and tested by att_req_send_process() to pick a free channel — so the lookup reads through a NULL pointer as soon as it visits an idle channel. Every other chan->req user in the file already guards the pointer. The lookup is reached from the public bt_gatt_cancel() API and, more importantly, from the host itself: bt_gatt_unsubscribe() calls bt_gatt_cancel() while a subscribe CCC write is still outstanding (BT_GATT_SUBSCRIBE_FLAG_WRITE_PENDING), and call_notify_cb_and_maybe_unsubscribe() in subsys/bluetooth/host/gatt.c invokes bt_gatt_unsubscribe() from the RX path whenever an application notify callback returns BT_GATT_ITER_STOP. A malicious or malfunctioning peer can hold the trigger window open by withholding the ATT Write Response to the CCC write and then sending a notification for the subscribed handle. With CONFIG_BT_EATT the traversal is very likely to meet an idle sibling channel, since ATT channels are prepended to the list and a channel opened after the pending request was sent is visited first. The dereference is a read of a small constant offset from address zero, so the impact is availability only: no memory corruption, no attacker-chosen address and no information disclosure. On platforms and configurations where a near-NULL read traps — TrustZone non-secure images, MMU targets, native_sim, or builds with CONFIG_NULL_POINTER_EXCEPTION_DETECTION_MPU/_DWT — the fault occurs in the Bluetooth RX context and results in a fatal error and device reset. On a plain Cortex-M build with the vector table mapped at address 0 and null-pointer detection disabled (the default) the read succeeds and the defect is inert. The fix adds an explicit chan->req != NULL test to the channel traversal and additionally rejects a NULL user_data argument, which would otherwise have matched, and cancelled, an unrelated request.
Severity: 5.3 | MEDIUM

cvefeed.io Latest.title: CVE-2026-93671 - Out-of-bounds read logging a mismatched Sec-WebSocket-Accept header in the Zephyr websocket client
cvefeed.io Latest.description:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-93671
Published : Nov. 16, 2026, 10:18 p.m. | 2 hours, 20 minutes ago
Description :The websocket client's HTTP header callback on_header_value() in subsys/net/lib/websocket/websocket.c receives the Sec-WebSocket-Accept header value as a pointer/length pair from the HTTP parser. The referenced bytes live inside the application-supplied receive buffer and are not NUL terminated. When the received value did not match the expected accept key, the pointer was passed directly to a %s conversion in a NET_DBG() call, so the logging code measured the string with strlen() and read on past the end of the header value looking for a terminator. The value is supplied by the peer during the WebSocket handshake, before any application-level authentication, so a malicious or man-in-the-middle server reached over a ws:// (or otherwise attacker-terminated) connection can trigger the mismatch branch at will simply by answering with a wrong accept key. By sizing the response so the header value ends at the tail of the buffer passed to websocket_connect() as wreq->tmp_buf, the peer can make the scan run off the end of that buffer and into adjacent memory. The defective log statement is compiled in only when websocket debug logging is enabled (CONFIG_NET_WEBSOCKET_LOG_LEVEL_DBG=y, or CONFIG_LOG_DEFAULT_LEVEL=4); it is absent from a default build, which bounds exposure to diagnostic configurations. The consequence is an out-of-bounds read whose contents are emitted to the log stream: memory adjacent to the receive buffer is disclosed wherever the device's logs are collected or displayed. On targets where the memory following the buffer is not mapped, the scan can instead fault and terminate the connection or thread. No out-of-bounds write occurs, so there is no integrity impact. The fix copies at most sizeof(got) - 1 bytes of the parser-provided slice into a bounded stack buffer, NUL terminates the copy, and logs that instead, so the formatter never reads beyond the bytes the parser actually offered.
Severity: 3.7 | LOW

cvefeed.io Latest.title: CVE-2026-93670 - Out-of-bounds write in the DesignWare I3C driver when the device address table is full
cvefeed.io Latest.description:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-93670
Published : Nov. 16, 2026, 10:18 p.m. | 2 hours, 20 minutes ago
Description :The Synopsys DesignWare I3C controller driver (drivers/i3c/i3c_dw.c) tracks free Device Address Table (DAT) slots with get_free_pos(), which signals an exhausted table by returning -1. The helper declared its return type as uint8_t, so the sentinel was truncated to 255, and both consumers (dw_i3c_attach_device() and dw_i3c_i2c_attach_device()) also stored it in a uint8_t before testing if (pos < 0) — a comparison that is never true for an unsigned value. The exhaustion guard was therefore inert in every build. With the guard defeated, an attach attempted on a full DAT proceeds with pos == 255: it writes data->dw_i3c_i2c_priv_data[255].id, more than 200 bytes past the end of the 32-element dw_i3c_i2c_priv_data array and past the end of struct dw_i3c_data; it stores the resulting out-of-bounds address in desc->controller_priv, from which later detach, reattach and IBI operations read the slot index back; and it performs a 32-bit MMIO store 1020 bytes beyond the hardware DAT base, outside the table the controller reports. The attach still returns success, so the upper layer believes the device is bound. The DAT is smaller than the software array (its depth is read from DEVICE_ADDR_TABLE_POINTER, commonly 8 or 16 entries), so exhaustion is reachable. In a dual-role build (CONFIG_I3C_DUAL_ROLE with CONFIG_I3C_USE_IBI) acting as a secondary controller, the attach count is supplied by the bus's active controller: i3c_sec_handoffed() attaches one device per entry of the received DEFTGTS list, so a hostile or malfunctioning controller on the local I3C bus that declares more targets than the local DAT depth triggers the condition once per surplus entry. Exhaustion can also be reached from a devicetree that declares more devices than the table holds, or by repeated i3c attach shell commands. Impact is bounded: the out-of-bounds store is a single byte of fixed value at a fixed displacement, with no attacker-chosen data or offset, so the realistic outcomes are corruption of neighbouring static driver state, writes into reserved controller registers, and inconsistent driver bookkeeping (a crash or a wedged I3C bus) rather than a controllable memory-write primitive. The attack vector is the local chip-to-chip I3C bus; there is no network-reachable path.
Severity: 3.5 | LOW

cvefeed.io Latest.title: CVE-2026-93669 - NULL pointer dereference in the ITE IT8xxx2 SHI host-command backend when a host transaction arrives before backend initialization
cvefeed.io Latest.description:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-93669
Published : Nov. 16, 2026, 10:18 p.m. | 2 hours, 20 minutes ago
Description :The ITE IT8xxx2 SHI host-command backend in subsys/mgmt/ec_host_cmd/backends/ec_host_cmd_backend_shi_ite.c arms the SPI peripheral before its receive context exists. shi_ite_init_registers() sets the state machine to SHI_STATE_READY_TO_RECV and calls irq_enable() while the device initializes at POST_KERNEL priority CONFIG_KERNEL_INIT_PRIORITY_DEFAULT (40), but data->rx_ctx and data->tx are only assigned later by shi_ite_backend_init(), which ec_host_cmd_init() invokes at CONFIG_EC_HOST_CMD_INIT_PRIORITY (default 80). If the attached host processor starts a SPI transaction inside that window, the Rx-valid-length interrupt fires, shi_ite_int_handler() passes its state check and calls shi_ite_parse_header(), which stores the host-derived request length through the still-NULL data->rx_ctx. On the IT8xxx2 low addresses are not backed by RAM, and with CONFIG_NULL_POINTER_EXCEPTION_DETECTION_PMP the first bytes of the address space are explicitly made inaccessible, so the store raises a fatal access fault in interrupt context. The window widens further when CONFIG_EC_HOST_CMD_INITIALIZE_AT_BOOT is disabled and the application calls ec_host_cmd_init() itself. The result is a kernel panic on the embedded controller: with Zephyr's default fatal handler the CPU halts, so the controller stops servicing host commands until a hardware reset. Because the trigger is traffic from the attached host processor -- an untrusted peer from the controller firmware's point of view -- software on that host can provoke the fault by forcing a controller reset and issuing transactions during the reboot, turning a recoverable reset into a persistent outage. Impact is limited to availability: the faulting address is fixed and not attacker-chosen, so no memory-corruption primitive follows. The fix leaves the interface at SHI_STATE_DISABLED with the interrupt masked during device init, moves irq_enable() into shi_ite_backend_init() after the buffers are published, and makes shi_ite_int_handler() reject a NULL data->rx_ctx while write-clearing IT83XX_SPI_ISR and IT83XX_SPI_RX_VLISR so that an unexpected early interrupt cannot storm.
Severity: 4.7 | MEDIUM

cvefeed.io Latest.title: CVE-2026-93668 - Bluetooth BR/EDR SDP server blocks the Bluetooth workqueue indefinitely when the SDP buffer pool is empty
cvefeed.io Latest.description:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-93668
Published : Nov. 16, 2026, 10:18 p.m. | 2 hours, 21 minutes ago
Description :The Bluetooth Classic SDP server in subsys/bluetooth/host/classic/sdp.c allocated every response PDU through bt_sdp_create_pdu(), which expands to bt_l2cap_create_pdu() and therefore uses a K_FOREVER timeout. The allocation is made from sdp_pool, a fixed pool holding only CONFIG_BT_MAX_CONN buffers (one in the default configuration) that is shared with the SDP client role. When the pool is empty the call blocks without a bound. The allocation is reached from bt_sdp_recv() on the Bluetooth host's RX context: the bt_workq "BT RX WQ" workqueue in the default configuration since v3.1.0, and the dedicated "BT RX" thread before that. This context processes all normal-priority HCI events and all received ACL data. The SDP L2CAP server is registered on PSM 0x0001 with no security requirement (BT_SECURITY_L0), so an unpaired, unauthenticated BR/EDR peer within radio range of a connectable device can drive it. Every malformed or unrecognised SDP PDU reaches send_err_rsp(), and the sdp_svc_search_req(), sdp_svc_att_req() and sdp_svc_search_att_req() handlers allocate as well, so a short burst of pipelined requests drains the pool and parks the RX context in the blocking allocation. A pool buffer is released only once its response has been sent, and a peer that withholds baseband acknowledgements keeps the controller's buffers for the link full, so the response is never sent. While the RX context is blocked, the entire Bluetooth host, for all connections and both LE and BR/EDR, stops processing normal-priority HCI events and received data. In most affected releases the stall is permanent. Queued PDUs are freed only by connection or channel teardown, which waits for the normal-priority Disconnection Complete handler, and that handler runs on the blocked RX context, so the host does not recover without a reset. In v3.7.0 through v4.1.x the TX processor discards the queued response once the link supervision timeout drops the connection, so each stall ends at that timeout, but the peer can reconnect and repeat it for as long as it stays in range. The impact is limited to availability; no memory corruption or information disclosure is involved. The fix adds sdp_svc_create_pdu() using K_NO_WAIT, pre-allocates the response buffer once in bt_sdp_recv(), stashes the request in sdp->recv_pending when no buffer is available, and retries it from a work handler once a buffer is freed by the pool destroy callback.
Severity: 6.5 | MEDIUM

cvefeed.io Latest.title: CVE-2026-93667 - Function pointer type confusion in Zephyr Virtual L2 when a VLAN-tagged frame finds no handling virtual interface
cvefeed.io Latest.description:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-93667
Published : Nov. 16, 2026, 10:18 p.m. | 2 hours, 21 minutes ago
Description :The Virtual L2 receive handler virtual_recv() in subsys/net/l2/virtual/virtual.c ends with a fall-through path meant for a virtual interface that has nothing attached below it: it takes net_if_get_device(iface)->api, treats it as a struct virtual_interface_api, and calls api->recv(iface, pkt). That handler is however also invoked with a non-virtual interface: ethernet_recv() in subsys/net/l2/ethernet/ethernet.c deliberately passes the Ethernet interface so that a tagged frame can be dispatched over the VLAN interfaces attached to it. For an Ethernet interface dev->api is a struct ethernet_api, whose layout only shares the leading struct net_if_api, so the slot read as recv is actually get_config() (default) or get_capabilities() (when CONFIG_NET_STATISTICS_ETHERNET is enabled). The fall-through is reached whenever no attached virtual interface claims the frame - most simply when the VLAN interface owning the frame's tag exists but is administratively down, since net_eth_get_vlan_iface() resolves the tag without checking link state while virtual_recv() skips interfaces that are not up. Any host able to place an 802.1Q-tagged Ethernet frame on the same link can then trigger the mistyped indirect call; no authentication, IP reachability or user interaction is required, because the frame is consumed at L2 before any address check. The resulting call passes a struct net_if where the driver expects a struct device and a struct net_pkt where it expects a struct net_if , with the callee's remaining parameters left as whatever the call site happens to leave in the argument registers. Driver implementations dereference these values: get_capabilities() typically reads dev->config/dev->data (a wild read through a non-pointer field of struct net_if), and get_config() implementations write through the uninitialized struct ethernet_config * argument. The practical impact is undefined behaviour in the network RX path - crashes and uncontrolled memory corruption - plus mis-handling of the packet when a capability bitmask is returned as a net_verdict. The attacker controls neither the corrupted address nor the value written, so this is a denial-of-service and memory-corruption issue rather than a controllable write primitive. The same defective fall-through is reachable through any_recv() in subsys/net/l2/dummy/any/any.c, which passes a dummy interface whose struct dummy_api is shorter than the offset read, producing an out-of-bounds read of the driver's API object followed by an indirect call. The fix drops any packet whose interface is not a Virtual L2 interface, closing both entry points.
Severity: 5.9 | MEDIUM

cvefeed.io Latest.title: CVE-2026-93666 - Bluetooth Classic SDP client can deadlock the Bluetooth workqueue on buffer allocation
cvefeed.io Latest.description:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-93666
Published : Nov. 16, 2026, 10:18 p.m. | 2 hours, 21 minutes ago
Description :The Bluetooth Classic SDP client built its outgoing request PDUs with bt_sdp_create_pdu(), which allocates from the sdp_pool net-buf pool with a K_FOREVER timeout and no failure handling, in sdp_client_ss_search(), sdp_client_sa_search() and sdp_client_ssa_search() in subsys/bluetooth/host/classic/sdp.c. All of these run on the Bluetooth workqueue bt_workq (via sdp_client_work_handler(), the L2CAP sdp_client_connected() callback, or the continuation-state follow-up from a received response), which is the same single thread that dispatches incoming HCI ACL and event traffic, drives L2CAP, and performs connection and channel teardown. sdp_pool holds only CONFIG_BT_MAX_CONN buffers (one by default) and is shared with the SDP server role. An unauthenticated peer within BR/EDR range can drive both halves of the trigger. The SDP L2CAP server is registered at BT_SECURITY_L0, so any inbound SDP request makes the device allocate the pool's buffer for a response, which is held until the controller has transmitted it. The same peer can then cause a client request to be issued while the pool is empty: in-tree profiles start SDP discovery from inbound connection callbacks (for example hfp_hf_accept() calls bt_sdp_discover() through hfp_hf_create(), and hfp_ag.c mirrors this), and a peer acting as an SDP server can force repeated client requests by answering with partial responses carrying continuation state. With the pool empty, the allocation blocks uninterruptibly and freezes the entire Bluetooth host. The stall becomes permanent when the release of the outstanding buffer itself depends on the blocked workqueue: if the link carrying the queued PDU is dropped or stalls, hci_disconn_complete() and the L2CAP channel cleanup that purges the channel TX queue are themselves bt_workq work items, so the buffer is never returned. The result is an unrecoverable denial of service of all Bluetooth functionality until reboot; there is no memory-safety, confidentiality or integrity impact. The fix allocates client PDUs with K_NO_WAIT via a new sdp_client_create_pdu(), propagates -ENOBUFS, parks the session on a new SDP_CLIENT_FLAG_WAIT_FOR_TX_BUF flag, and adds an sdp_pool destructor that re-submits the SDP client worker when a buffer becomes available. Note that the SDP server role still allocated from the same pool with K_FOREVER at this commit; that path was addressed separately.
Severity: 5.3 | MEDIUM
